inventory.note: What the town ALREADY CONTAINS, in the words a brief would use. Read by every worker before it builds. This list is the direct antidote to the previous loop's terminal failure mode: nine consecutive iterations that each surveyed the world, found everything already existed, and exited.
courtyard: walled garden with an organic bed ring
four arch entrances (two TUNNEL, two SLOT)
planting CA with 11 species and bloom stages
seeds that spread from mature neighbours, and beds that crowd out and die back with age
rain that accelerates every growth term
lane: washing lines strung over the lane
market day every 4th day with three stalls

washing that comes in before the rain: the rope stays strung and garments leave one at a time on per-garment thresholds and ~1.6s fades, driven by weatherComing() and a dusk ramp — never all in one frame
street: cross street with two footways, roadway, curbs
allotment block with 21 plots, timber fence, gates, shed
gardeners who walk in through the gate to a real bed cell and kneel to plant it
an alley cut through the block

allotment harvest cycle — a mature 3x2 plot is lifted whole by the kneeling 'allot' gardener (harvestPlot), rests fallow 12-20s on bAge (which doubles as the fallow clock on an empty bed; dieback now zeroes it), then is re-sown as a row: first drill at 0.055, the other five at 0.30 under plotCrop(), so it comes back under one crop and usually a different one

spawnAllotAgent() — the allotments' own arrival source, rate 0.01 + 0.16*ripePlots()/17, gated daylight>0.3 and day>=1, cap 3. The crop calls its own picker: ~1.1 gardeners/day and ~1 plot cleared/day, against 0.06-0.22/day when they only came out of spawnLaneAgent's 0.36-0.42 roll band
gardeners work 1-3 rows a visit (a.rows, 0.55 to continue) and walk out carrying a basket of the crop (a.crop, drawn in drawPerson)
census planting.harvested — cumulative cells picked; the only field separating a picked plot from a died-back one
plaza: quay along the river with benches

an arrival source of its own: spawnEastAgent() with eastCap/eastRate, agents flagged a.east and excluded from laneCount — they enter by the alley cut (plaza), the north end of the quay (quay) or the park gate arch (towpath, church green), visit one existing stop and leave the way they came; eastOpen() (daylight > 0.16) stops new arrivals, gets sitters up, and sends the walk home at 1.55x
census life.inEast — walkers east of the allotments, a partition of onStreet
river: pigeons that flush off the church belfry when the bell rings, from a finite roost that refills
sky: cloud cover as one slow rate-capped scalar (cloudCover()) — fronts build over ~half a day and break up after rain · drifting cloud banks that fade in as cover thickens · rain gated on cover, so it never rains from a clear sky · sun and moon veiled · stars put out · roof key light flattened · overcast ticker lines

weatherComing(): one ramped predicate for 'rain is coming', off cloudCover() and damped by daylight so overcast nights (which cannot rain) read 0. Three readers at their own trigger points on the same scalar
life: walkers with itineraries, courtyard and street
eastern itineraries that already exist: plaza bench, fountain gaze, quay rail, quay bench, towpath, church green, allotment plot
café sitters who claim and release a table
a clock that strikes and a church bell that answers
walkers who break stride and look up while the bell is ringing (a.listen)
agents that notice each other: two who pass within 0.9–1.6 cells may stop, turn and talk a few seconds (greetPass, a.greet, chatCool), then walk on — ~2 conversations a minute
butterflies drift to their flower at a capped 3 cells/s instead of lunging across the courtyard
street sitters who read the sky: new sits refused above weatherComing() 0.42, existing sitters released over 0.55..0.88 off a stable per-agent a.wary (courtyard sitters excluded)
umbrellas that go up on the approach (weatherComing() 0.62..1.17, so ~30% never open one), put away below 0.42 and cleared when the rain stops

openCues.note: The town stops changing after ~15 real minutes. maturity() caps at day 8 and richness() at day 16; at a 55 s day that is 14.7 minutes, after which every progression term is pinned at 1. There is no season and no later act. This is the rung-4 lever that would reopen the whole board. state.mjs rewrites state.json with JSON.stringify(...,2), which explodes every inline array onto its own lines — the first write after a hand-edited file produced a 353-line diff for two inventory entries. HARNESS, not town: no worker brief can fix it. Now benign in practice because the file is already fully exploded, so every subsequent write is a clean diff. Downgraded from noise-risk to a cosmetic note; close it if it has not bitten by pass #12.
The town still casts hard sun shadows under full overcast — drawSunMoon veils the disc, but the ~6 SUN[0]/SUN[2] shadow call sites use fixed alphas.
Rain requires daylight>0.15, so a heavy front peaking overnight builds full cover, never rains, and breaks by morning — overcast nights are commoner than rain.
chatCool is decremented only inside greetPass(); an early-out there would freeze the cooldown
East agents retrace their inbound route exactly, so arrivals sharing a gate walk single-file; would queue if eastCap rose much above 7

People DO cross the bridge: the lane IS the bridge (RIVER_X0 114 to RIVER_X1 127, carried at LANE_N_Y 66.4), and the `green` itinerary routes walkers out to PARK_GATE at x=134, so every far-bank visitor walks over the water. RUNLOG.jsonl records secs=0, costUsd=0, turns=0, tokens=null on every worker row (iters 2-5); only the manager row carries real numbers. The exact metric that killed the previous loop — cost per iteration climbing while output stays flat — is therefore unmeasurable for the workers, and stall.mjs is averaging $0.28/iter off the one manager row that has data. HARNESS, not town: needs run-loop.sh or runlog.mjs to capture the worker session cost. Flagged to the human at pass #5.

Courtyard sitters (picnic, sitter kinds) do not read the sky — only a.street agents do. Their sit is assigned at a waypoint with no route left, so refusing it would despawn them mid-lawn; extending the effect inland needs routeToExit() on refusal.
The allotment block is 17 plots, not 21: buildGrid excludes x>=84 && y>=42 for the pond corner. Brief b6 and the inventory both said 21.
ripePlots() rescans 102 cells every spawn tick (1/s) to set an arrival rate — the first place a spawn rate reads the CA. Free at this size; cache it on the CA tick if anything else wants the pattern.

watch.note: The whole east half is fed by a single spawnLaneAgent roll under one laneCap. Anything you add out there competes for that one budget — check whether your feature needs its own before you conclude nobody uses it. The bands, measured: cross-street diversion 0.30 of all spawns, then market 0.24, kiosk 0.18, café 0.26, allotment to 0.48, plaza to 0.48, quay 0.48-0.53, green 0.53-0.58. laneCap peaks at 9 in full daylight.

An empty-looking place is a budget question before it is a content question. Twice at pass #0 a plausible 'the town lacks X' turned out to be 'the town has X and you rarely see it' — the allotment gardeners and every eastern destination both exist. Grep for the feature before briefing it, and if it exists, ask how often it fires.

cloudCover() (added #3) is a slow world scalar with exactly ONE reader — the rain roll. It hands the town ~27 s of warning that rain is coming and nothing else in the file reads it. Any future weather work should ask whether it can read cover instead of reading `raining`, which is a boolean that flips in a single frame.
